# CORBA Calc TP (ENISO)
This project contains the IDL and Java skeletons for the CORBA "Calc" example from the TP.
Files added:
- `calc.idl` — IDL describing module `eniso`, exception `DivByZeroException` and interface `Calc`. - `src/CalcImpl.java` — servant implementation extending `CalcPOA` (requires IDL-generated classes). - `src/Serveur.java` — ORB/POA initialization, registers `Calc` under the name `MyCalc`. - `src/Client.java` — Looks up `MyCalc` and calls `div(8,3)`. - `src/ServeurDeNom.java` — convenience helper to launch `orbd` (platform dependent).
Quick steps (Windows PowerShell) — assumes a Java ORB is installed and `idlj` and `orbd` are on PATH.
1. Generate Java stubs from IDL
```powershell cd "${PWD}" idlj -fall calc.idl -d src ```
This generates the `eniso` Java package (Calc, CalcHelper, CalcPOA, DivByZeroException, etc.) in `src`.
2. Compile Java sources
```powershell cd src javac -d . *.java eniso/*.java ```
3. Start the naming service (orbd)
Either run it manually in a separate shell:
```powershell orbd -ORBInitialPort 5000 -ORBInitialHost localhost ```
or use the small Java helper (may return immediately):
```powershell java ServeurDeNom ```
4. Start the server (in another shell)
```powershell cd src java Serveur -ORBInitialPort 5000 -ORBInitialHost localhost ```
5. Start the client (in another shell)
```powershell cd src java Client -ORBInitialPort 5000 -ORBInitialHost localhost ```
Notes and troubleshooting
- The code relies on a CORBA ORB (the JDK used to include a reference ORB in older releases; modern setups may require installing a third-party ORB such as JacORB or configuring the vendor ORB). - If `idlj` or `orbd` are not available, install a JDK with IDL tools or get an ORB implementation. - If compilation fails because `org.omg` packages are missing, ensure your Java runtime includes CORBA APIs or use an ORB distribution that supplies them.
Next steps you might want me to do:
- Run `idlj` and generate the stubs here and add them to the repo so the project compiles. - Compile the sources and run a smoke test (if you have ORB installed in this environment).
## Getting Started
Welcome to the VS Code Java world. Here is a guideline to help you get started to write Java code in Visual Studio Code.
## Folder Structure
The workspace contains two folders by default, where:
- `src`: the folder to maintain sources - `lib`: the folder to maintain dependencies
Meanwhile, the compiled output files will be generated in the `bin` folder by default.
> If you want to customize the folder structure, open `.vscode/settings.json` and update the related settings there.
## Dependency Management
The `JAVA PROJECTS` view allows you to manage your dependencies. More details can be found [here](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-java-dependency#manage-dependencies). # CORBA-Part-1

## ⚠️ IMPORTANT: CORBA Compatibility Issue
**Your current Java version (22) does not include CORBA support!**
CORBA was deprecated in Java 9 and completely removed in Java 11+. The `orbd` and `idlj` commands are not available in modern Java versions.
### Quick Fix: Install Java 8
1. **Download Java 8 (JDK 8)**: - Oracle: https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/javase/javase8-archive-downloads.html - Or Adoptium (OpenJDK): https://adoptium.net/temurin/releases/?version=8
2. **Install and set JAVA_HOME**: ```bash # After installation, verify: java -version # Should show version 1.8.x ```
3. **Continue with the TP using Java 8** - all commands below will work!
